units.sourceHTML: 5.8 Escape Sequences - specifying special characters

units.text: Until this chapter, we have only encountered escapes of the form ‘⟦0⟧’, which tell ⟦1⟧ not to interpret the circumflex as a special character, but rather to take it literally. For example, ‘⟦2⟧’ matches a single asterisk rather than zero or more backslashes.
units.sourceHTML: Until this chapter, we have only encountered escapes of the form ‘\^’, which tell sed not to interpret the circumflex as a special character, but rather to take it literally. For example, ‘\*’ matches a single asterisk rather than zero or more backslashes.

units.text: This chapter introduces another kind of escape⟦0⟧⟦1⟧6⟦2⟧⟦3⟧—that is, escapes that are applied to a character or sequence of characters that ordinarily are taken literally, and that ⟦4⟧ replaces with a special character. This provides a way of encoding non-printable characters in patterns in a visible manner. There is no restriction on the appearance of non-printing characters in a ⟦5⟧ script but when a script is being prepared in the shell or by text editing, it is usually easier to use one of the following escape sequences than the binary character it represents:

This provides a way of encoding non-printable characters in patterns in a visible manner. There is no restriction on the appearance of non-printing characters in a sed script but when a script is being prepared in the shell or by text editing, it is usually easier to use one of the following escape sequences than the binary character it represents:

units.text: The list of these escapes is:
Produces or matches a ⟦0⟧BEL⟦1⟧ character, that is an “alert” (⟦2⟧ASCII⟦3⟧ 7).
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a BEL character, that is an “alert” (ASCII 7).

units.text: Produces or matches a form feed (⟦0⟧ASCII⟦1⟧ 12).
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a form feed (ASCII 12).

units.text: Produces or matches a carriage return (⟦0⟧ASCII⟦1⟧ 13).
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a carriage return (ASCII 13).

units.text: Produces or matches a horizontal tab (⟦0⟧ASCII⟦1⟧ 9).
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a horizontal tab (ASCII 9).

units.text: Produces or matches a so called “vertical tab” (⟦0⟧ASCII⟦1⟧ 11).
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a so called “vertical tab” (ASCII 11).

units.text: Produces or matches ⟦0⟧⟦1⟧CONTROL⟦2⟧-⟦3⟧⟦4⟧, where ⟦5⟧ is any character. The precise effect of ‘⟦6⟧’ is as follows: if ⟦7⟧ is a lower case letter, it is converted to upper case. Then bit 6 of the character (hex 40) is inverted. Thus ‘⟦8⟧’ becomes hex 1A, but ‘⟦9⟧’ becomes hex 3B, while ‘⟦10⟧’ becomes hex 7B.
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches CONTROL-x, where x is any character. The precise effect of ‘\cx’ is as follows: if x is a lower case letter, it is converted to upper case. Then bit 6 of the character (hex 40) is inverted. Thus ‘\cz’ becomes hex 1A, but ‘\c{’ becomes hex 3B, while ‘\c;’ becomes hex 7B.

units.text: Produces or matches a character whose decimal ⟦0⟧ASCII⟦1⟧ value is ⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a character whose decimal ASCII value is xxx.

units.text: Produces or matches a character whose octal ⟦0⟧ASCII⟦1⟧ value is ⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a character whose octal ASCII value is xxx.

units.text: Produces or matches a character whose hexadecimal ⟦0⟧ASCII⟦1⟧ value is ⟦2⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Produces or matches a character whose hexadecimal ASCII value is xx.

units.text: ‘⟦0⟧’ (backspace) was omitted because of the conflict with the existing “word boundary” meaning.
units.sourceHTML: ‘\b’ (backspace) was omitted because of the conflict with the existing “word boundary” meaning.

units.text: All the escapes introduced here are GNU extensions, with the exception of ⟦0⟧. In basic regular expression mode, setting ⟦1⟧ disables them inside bracket expressions.
units.sourceHTML: All the escapes introduced here are GNU extensions, with the exception of \n. In basic regular expression mode, setting POSIXLY_CORRECT disables them inside bracket expressions.

nonProse: Command/flag literals and pure code/output examples retained; explanatory dt labels and italic pre descriptions extracted too; no unhandled prose text.
